passage:
Coach's note, Tuesday. Ujjwal stayed after cricket practice to ask if he could talk. He said his partner Kishore has been upset whenever he texts teammates or goes for tea with them, and he now feels watched, as if every message needs an explanation.

He told me he had already reassured Kishore once, plainly: he cares about him and nothing is going on. He said he had thought about deleting some chats to avoid arguments, then decided against it. "If I hide people, I'm the one shrinking," he said, frowning at his bat handle.

He plans to keep his friendships and stay kind. I did not advise beyond listening. I mentioned the college counsellor, in case the upset keeps going or he finds it wearing him down.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal do after cricket practice on Tuesday?
qa.a: He stayed after cricket practice to ask if he could talk to the coach.

qa.q: What does Ujjwal's remark 'If I hide people, I'm the one shrinking' suggest he is thinking?
qa.a: It suggests he sees that hiding his friends to keep the peace would cost him his own freedom, so he is not willing to trade it away.

qa.q: What could Ujjwal do if Kishore's upset keeps going even after he has reassured him?
qa.a: Stay kind but keep his friendships, and talk to a trusted person such as the college counsellor about how the pattern is affecting him.

qa.q: How might Kishore see the situation from where he stands?
qa.a: He may be feeling insecure and left out when Ujjwal is with teammates, so he may not yet see that his upset makes Ujjwal feel watched.

grounding: Shows a partner upset about friendships, the person feeling watched, reassuring once and refusing to hide people.
